mutants.label: quoted-material: [control] placeholder text renamed
mutants.why: The placeholder only ever reaches COMPLETION_CLAIM.search. Both texts open with '[' and close with ']' (identical \b, \s and $ context on either side) and no claim alternative starts with a letter inside 'quoted' or 'elided' at a word boundary, so no input matches under one and not the other. Holds for any message; it would stop holding only if a test imported _own_words and compared its text.

mutants.label: quoted-material: [control] line rule's trailing $ dropped
mutants.why: The pattern has MULTILINE but not DOTALL, so a greedy .* stops at the line's end and $ is already true there; dropping it removes a redundant assertion on every input.

mutants.label: quoted-material: [control] line rule runs before the fence rule
mutants.why: A line the line rule replaces starts with > or |, so it can be neither a fence opener nor a closer (the CommonMark opener and the closer both start with a backtick or tilde run at the line start). The new info-string rule reads only an opener line, and the closer rule only a closer line, so a replaced line is never read by either. The fence rule replaces every body line wholesale. So the two orders produce the same text for any message. The line rule's replacement, [quoted], starts with neither a backtick nor a tilde.
